$comment: Single source of truth for platform publishing specs. Every value is either verified against
the platform's own documentation or explicitly marked unverified. A skill may never present an
unverified value to a client as fact.
safe_zone has two tiers on purpose. Meta publishes 14%/35%/6% for Stories and Reels, but that
is the figure for the ADS unit, which carries a call-to-action button and disclaimer space an
organic story does not. Meta publishes no organic-only number. So: 'hard' is the ads-grade
keep-out and nothing that carries the message may enter it; 'soft' is the wider bound where
deliberately dimmed texture may sit and be covered without loss. Neither tier is a guess
dressed as a measurement — the hard tier is Meta's published number, the soft tier is a design
The 250/1670 bound used before this file existed did NOT come from Meta. It was a widely
repeated third-party figure, and content built against it sits 405px inside Meta's own
verification_note: Values marked unverified could not be traced to the platform's own documentation. Treat them as working assumptions, never as published fact.

render_targets.$comment: The four canvases the engine renders today. Each names the surfaces it serves.

safe_zone.basis: hard = Meta published 14% top / 35% bottom / 6% sides for Stories and Reels ads; soft = design decision for dimmed texture only
feed images carry no persistent platform UI over the image itself

vertical-feed.note: Meta's current recommended upload for 4:5 is 1440x1800. 1080x1350 is the same ratio, still valid, and displays identically because ratio drives the crop; it is simply no longer top-of-spec.

safe_zone.basis: no persistent overlay on feed images

horizontal.note: LinkedIn's lead recommendation for a single image is 1200x627 at 1.91:1. 1200x630 is within tolerance.

file.note: the Content Publishing API accepts JPEG only; width is auto-scaled between 320 and 1440

caption.note: a line break forces truncation at the end of the first line

reel.safe_zone_note: the right-side action rail is widely reported to eat further into the right margin; Meta publishes no separate number for it

duration.note: 20 minutes is the technical maximum; beyond 3 minutes Meta states reels are not recommended to non-followers. Two different numbers for two different purposes.

carousel.orientation_note: one orientation is chosen before adding media and applies to the whole set; the API crops to the first image, default 1:1
carousel.caption: one caption for the whole carousel, not per slide

alternatives.note: vertical is mobile-only and not the lead recommendation

multi_image.layout_note: layout is driven by image 1: landscape or shorter than 4:3 sits on top with the rest in a row below; portrait or taller sits left with the rest stacked right

document.$comment: This is LinkedIn's carousel mechanism. There is no separate multi-image carousel object; the standalone Carousel ad UI was retired (reported ~Dec 2023, unverified).

video.audio: aac or mpeg4, sample rate under 64kHz

duration.note: TikTok's own live help article states 60s recorded in-app and 3 minutes uploaded, which contradicts the 10 and 60 minute figures widely cited elsewhere in its own ecosystem. This is an unresolved inconsistency in TikTok's documentation. Build against 3 minutes unless extended access is confirmed on the specific account.

safe_zone.note: TikTok publishes no numeric safe zone and states the safe area shrinks as the caption grows, pointing creators to a preview tool instead. Any specific pixel figure in circulation is third-party.

hashtags.warning: a cap of 5 (7 for some accounts) is reported from around August 2025 but could not be confirmed on any official TikTok page. Do not hardcode it — verify against a live account first.

shorts.categorization_note: square or vertical videos of 3 minutes or less are auto-categorized as Shorts

safe_zone.note: Google publishes downloadable transparent-PNG templates for Shorts ads but no numeric values

hashtags.hard_rule: more than 60 hashtags on a video causes every hashtag to be ignored

image.mixing_note: an animated GIF cannot be combined with other images; one GIF, alone

post.note: photo and GIF attachments do not count against the character limit

hashtags.note: X's own guidance recommends no more than 2 per post; there is no technical cap

min_recommended_resolution.note: this ratio is not 9:16, so it reads as a minimum source-quality floor rather than the display frame. Supply the highest-resolution 9:16 source available.

status.quality_warning: HD is not supported for Status; media is compressed and quality is reduced. Design knowing the asset will be recompressed.

changed_recently: Stories and Reels safe zone: Meta's current published figure is 14% top / 35% bottom / 6% sides. Most circulating guides still cite roughly 20% or 250px at the bottom. A render engine with 20% hard-coded under-clears by 15 percentage points.
Instagram and Facebook feed: 4:5 confirmed over 1:1, and the recommended upload resolution moved from 1080x1350 to 1440x1800 at the same ratio.
Instagram carousel: 20 slides in-app versus 10 via API is a hard current split and a common trap for automated publishers.
Instagram Reels technical maximum is now 20 minutes, while the organic reach ceiling stays at 3 minutes.
WhatsApp Status video is now 90 seconds, up from the historical 30-second segment cap.
YouTube Shorts moved from 60 seconds to 3 minutes (effective 2024-10-15). Do not design against the old ceiling.
LinkedIn's separate Carousel ad UI was reportedly retired around December 2023 in favour of Document posts (secondary source only).
